alerts.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 16 at 5:32PM MDT until August 16 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
alerts.description:
At 532 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 8 miles south of
Boyero, or 38 miles southeast of Limon, moving southeast at 10 mph.

HAZARD...Ping pong ball size hail and 60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect hail
damage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles. Expect wind
damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Mainly rural areas of Southeastern Lincoln County.

alerts.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 16 at 5:31PM MDT until August 16 at 8:30PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
alerts.description:
FFWBOU

The National Weather Service in Denver has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Lincoln County in east central Colorado...

* Until 830 PM MDT.

* At 531 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between
1 and 3.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts
of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the southern portions of the
warned area that are currently receiving heavy rain. Flash flooding
is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar and automated gauges.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, gulches,
roads, and poor drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Boyero.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Coon Creek, Rush Creek, Big Sandy Creek and Folger Gulch.

This replaces and expands the previous Flash Flood Warning for east
central Lincoln County.

alerts.headline: Flood Advisory issued August 16 at 5:21PM MDT until August 16 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Lincoln County in east central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 800 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 521 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Up to 0.5 inches of rain have
fallen.

- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 1.5 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Wild Horse Point.

alerts.headline: Flood Advisory issued August 16 at 5:08PM MDT until August 16 at 6:15PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
alerts.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southeastern Elbert County in east central Colorado...
Southern Lincoln County in east central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 615 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Stream flows are elevated.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 505 PM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated heavy rain due to thunderstorms. The storms were moving
southeast at 15 mph. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 2 inches of
rain have fallen.

- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Punkin Center, Karval, Forder, and Kutch.

- The Boyero area and Big Sandy Creek has been upgraded to a
Flash Flood Warning. See additional information in that bulletin.

alerts.title: I-70 Seibert-Stratton Roadway Improvements-139794
alerts.description: Between Exit 395: Flagler (3 miles west of the Seibert area) and Exit 412: Vona (2 miles east of the Seibert area) from Mile Point 401 to Mile Point 408.5. The left lane is closed due to road construction. There is a width limit in effect. Width limit 11'0". Until October 30, 2026 at about 7:00PM MDT. Full schedule below: • July 21, 7:00AM - October 30, 7:00PM Comment: Westbound I-70 traffic will shift to a 24/7 head-to-head traffic configuration, with one lane of traffic in each direction maintained on eastbound I-70. Caution: Watch for construction vehicles periodically pacing traffic and be prepared for narrowed lanes and changing traffic patterns through the work zone. Caution when entering and exiting the head-to-head traffic configuration and at the on- and off-ramps.
